chosen.premise: Golduck is described as faster than every Pokémon and every human swimming champion, even in rough seas.
chosen.hook: This Pokémon is officially described as the fastest swimmer of all.
chosen.visualIdea: Race Golduck against a human champion, fish Pokémon, and storm waves as each comparison appears.
chosen.note: A Golduck-specific superlative backed by multiple Pokédex entries: fastest among Pokémon, faster than human champions, and capable in stormy seas. The race comparisons are immediately visual.

candidates.visualIdea: Race Golduck against a human champion, fish Pokémon, and storm waves as each comparison appears.
candidates.note: A Golduck-specific superlative backed by multiple Pokédex entries: fastest among Pokémon, faster than human champions, and capable in stormy seas. The race comparisons are immediately visual.

candidates.premise: Golduck can keep swimming for two straight days by skillfully waving its long tail.
candidates.hook: Golduck can swim continuously for two entire days.
candidates.visualIdea: A day-night cycle spins around Golduck while its tail keeps paddling without stopping.
candidates.note: An unusually precise endurance claim with direct support. It is highly hookable, though the day-night visual is somewhat simpler and less dynamic than a competitive speed premise.

candidates.premise: Old tales say Golduck punished people who polluted its river by dragging them into the water.
candidates.hook: Defile Golduck's river, and old tales say it will drag you away.
candidates.visualIdea: A peaceful river turns ominous as shadowy hands pull a guilty figure beneath the surface.
candidates.note: Very distinctive folklore with strong atmosphere, but it rests on one entry and 'polluted' is an interpretation of 'defiled,' so the premise needs careful wording.

candidates.premise: At full swimming speed, Golduck's forehead glows—and that glow may unlock telekinesis or its full power.
candidates.hook: Golduck's forehead only starts glowing when it reaches full speed.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Golduck accelerating through water, its forehead lighting up before psychic energy bursts outward.
candidates.note: Strong visual transformation with several supporting entries, but the connection between full swimming speed, glowing, telekinesis, and total power is phrased as uncertain in the source.

candidates.premise: Golduck rescues people from wrecked ships, but also disables fast fish and quietly eats them.
candidates.hook: Golduck can be a shipwreck hero—or a terrifying underwater hunter.
candidates.visualIdea: Split the screen between Golduck pulling a survivor from waves and freezing a fish before eating it.
candidates.note: The hero-versus-predator contrast is compelling and well supported, but 'freezing' the fish overstates the source, which says Golduck brings them to a standstill.

candidates.premise: Golduck was over-hunted because people believed its red forehead granted supernatural powers.
candidates.hook: People hunted Golduck for the power they thought was inside its forehead.
candidates.visualIdea: Zoom from the red forehead to old hunters, then reveal that the glow is linked to psychic power.
candidates.note: The over-hunting detail is distinctive and directly supported, but the angle risks blurring a belief about supernatural power with Golduck's separate, uncertain psychic abilities.

rounds.request: Not applicable: fastest-swimmer is strong enough. Stronger alternatives would need an equally concrete, source-backed claim with either a sharper contradiction or a more measurable feat than being Pokémon's fastest swimmer.
